cards.front: Chorionicity must be determined by ultrasound (USS) at 11–14 weeks. Lambda sign = dichorionic; T sign = [___].
cards.context:
Chorionicity means placental sharing, and it drives twin-pregnancy risk more than zygosity. It is best assigned on first-trimester ultrasound scan (USS), before the inter-twin membrane becomes harder to interpret.

Lambda/twin-peak sign means dichorionic twins with placental tissue between membranes. T sign means monochorionic twins, who need closer surveillance for twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome.

cards.front: Transvaginal cervical length ≤25 mm at [___] weeks defines a 'short cervix' and substantially raises spontaneous preterm birth risk.
cards.context:
Use transvaginal ultrasound to confirm suspected short cervix. In the current WA pathway, low-risk screening starts with transabdominal assessment at the 18-20-week anatomy scan.

If transabdominal length is under 35 mm, confirm transvaginally. A confirmed 21-25 mm prompts vaginal progesterone and repeat scanning; shorter measurements need specialist review.

cards.front: Severe-range hypertension in pregnancy: SBP ≥[___] or DBP ≥110 mmHg; treat urgently to reduce maternal stroke risk.
cards.context:
Severe-range HTN in pregnancy (SBP ≥160 or DBP ≥110) is a hypertensive emergency — cerebral autoregulation breaks down, vasculature can't constrict adequately.

Treat acutely: IV hydralazine 5-10 mg, IV labetalol 20 mg (avoid in asthma), or oral nifedipine IR 10 mg — repeat q15-30 min until BP <160/110.

Don't aim for normotension: a precipitous drop collapses pressure-dependent uteroplacental perfusion, causing fetal distress. Target SBP 140-150, DBP 90-100 first hours, then oral (methyldopa, labetalol, nifedipine SR).

cards.front: Outpatient pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) empirical antibiotics: [___] (gonorrhoea) + doxycycline (chlamydia) + metronidazole (anaerobes).
cards.context:
PID is polymicrobial (Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, Mycoplasma genitalium, anaerobes); empirical antibiotics must cover all: ceftriaxone (gonorrhoea) + doxycycline (chlamydia) + metronidazole (anaerobes).

Threshold to treat is deliberately low (CDC): any sexually active woman with pelvic pain + cervical motion tenderness OR uterine tenderness OR adnexal tenderness — start treatment.

Most managed as outpatients (oral, review at 72 h); admit for IV if pregnant, severe, suspected tubo-ovarian abscess, no response to oral, or unable to tolerate oral. Sexual partner notification + treatment essential.

cards.front: Vitamin K prophylaxis (single [___] mg IM at birth) prevents haemorrhagic disease of the newborn.
cards.context:
Newborns are vitamin-K deficient (poor placental transfer, sterile gut, minimal K in breast milk), and factors II/VII/IX/X need K-dependent gamma-carboxylation — so deficiency causes haemorrhagic disease (VKDB).

Two forms: classical (days 2-7) and the more dangerous late-onset (2-12 weeks, 50% intracranial haemorrhage); standard prophylaxis 1 mg IM at birth, near-100% effective for both.

Oral regimens (3 doses over 4 weeks) are an alternative if parents decline IM, but need adherence and are less reliable for late VKDB. The 1992 IM-vit-K/leukaemia link has been refuted — document any refusal.

cards.front: EPDS interpretation thresholds: a total score of 13 is the cut-off for probable depression (full psychiatric assessment); scores of 10-12 are possible cases (repeat in 2-4 weeks); a positive response on the dedicated [___] item triggers immediate safety assessment regardless of total score.
cards.context:
EPDS is a 10-item self-report questionnaire (scored 0-30) validated for antenatal + postnatal screening.

Interpretation: <10 = low risk, routine follow-up; 10-12 = possible, repeat in 2-4 weeks; ≥13 = probable, full psychiatric assessment.

cards.front: Safer Baby Bundle: side-sleeping is recommended from 28 weeks because supine sleep doubles late stillbirth risk via [___] compression.
cards.context: The supine-sleep effect is mechanical — the gravid uterus compresses the IVC, halving venous return and dropping cardiac output enough to reduce uteroplacental perfusion.

cards.front: A low-lying placenta has its edge within 20 mm of the internal os without covering it; seen in ~5% at the second-trimester scan but only 0.5-1% remain low-lying at term as ~85% [___].
cards.context:
Low-lying placenta: placental edge within 20 mm of the internal cervical os but NOT covering it — found in ~5% of pregnancies at the second-trimester scan.

~85% resolve to a normal position by term as the lower segment develops, leaving only ~0.5-1% still low-lying at term. Placenta praevia: placenta covers or overlies the internal cervical os.

Unlike a low-lying placenta, true praevia seen at the second-trimester scan resolves far less reliably and should not be assumed to migrate away.

cards.front: Postnatal mood spectrum: baby blues peak at days 3-5 and self-resolve; postnatal depression peaks at 3-6 months. Screen with [___].
cards.context:
Postnatal mood disorders form a clinical spectrum and are separated by timing, severity and loss of reality testing.

Baby blues (70-80%, days 3-5, self-limiting tearfulness) — reassurance, support, monitoring.

Postnatal depression usually emerges later, often around 3-6 months, and is screened with the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS).

cards.front: In vasa praevia, fetal mortality exceeds [___]% if undiagnosed, but falls below 5% with elective caesarean at 35-36 weeks.
cards.context:
Vasa praevia: unprotected fetal vessels run across the cervical os — through membranes (Type 1, velamentous cord) or between placental lobes (Type 2, succenturiate/bilobed).

Undiagnosed mortality >50%; diagnosed + planned delivery (elective CS at 35-36 weeks before ROM) reduces to <5%.

Classical undiagnosed: painless bleeding at ROM + sinusoidal FHR → emergency CS.

cards.front: Pre-eclampsia diagnosis requires hypertension after [___] weeks PLUS new organ involvement (renal, hepatic, haematological, neurological, pulmonary, or placental).
cards.context:
2018 ISSHP/SOMANZ broadened pre-eclampsia from 'HTN + proteinuria' to 'HTN + ANY new organ involvement' — ~20% of pre-eclampsia has no significant proteinuria but still has organ dysfunction.

Organ systems to screen at every visit after 20 weeks: renal (urinalysis, creatinine), hepatic (LFTs), haematological (FBC, haemolysis film), neurological (visual, headache, hyperreflexia), pulmonary (oedema, dyspnoea).

cards.front: The classic triad of ruptured ectopic pregnancy is [___], vaginal bleeding, and unilateral pelvic pain.
cards.context:
The classic triad occurs in only about half of ectopic pregnancies; presentations may include GI symptoms, shoulder-tip pain or syncope.

Risk rises after previous ectopic, tubal damage or surgery, IVF, or pregnancy with an IUD in situ. Assess with TVUS and serial βhCG; an empty uterus above the local threshold is concerning but not diagnostic.

Rupture with instability needs urgent surgery. Stable, eligible patients with low βhCG and no fetal cardiac activity may be considered for methotrexate.

cards.front: Routine anti-D for Rh-negative women is given at [___] weeks and after sensitising events.
cards.context:
Routine anti-D prophylaxis (Australian schedule): 625 IU IM at 28 + 34 weeks + postnatal dose if cord blood Rh-positive. Prevents maternal sensitisation to fetal D-antigen.

Sensitising events trigger additional doses regardless of schedule: any vaginal bleeding ≥12 weeks, miscarriage requiring intervention, ectopic, molar, CVS, amnio, ECV, abdominal trauma, APH.

72-h window applies — give ASAP (partial protection up to 28 days). Check antibody screen before each dose; Kleihauer at delivery quantifies fetomaternal haemorrhage (1 vial covers ~6 mL fetal blood).

cards.front: Substance use in pregnancy requires a [___] approach with harm reduction; abrupt cessation of opioids or benzodiazepines is dangerous.
cards.context:
Abrupt opioid cessation in pregnancy precipitates withdrawal in mother and fetus, risking fetal distress and preterm labour. Abrupt benzo cessation risks maternal seizures.

Frame as non-judgemental harm reduction — women who feel judged stop attending antenatal care.

cards.front: There is currently no effective [___] programme for ovarian cancer. CA-125 is non-specific and most cases present at advanced stage.
cards.context:
CA-125 is non-specific (elevated in endometriosis, PID, liver disease, pregnancy) and TVUS alone has poor specificity.

The lack of screening means most cases present at advanced stage (III/IV), contributing to the high mortality. BRCA carriers should be offered risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy.

cards.front: ECV for breech is offered from 36 weeks (nulliparous) or 37 weeks (multiparous); overall success ~[___]%.
cards.context:
ECV is manual rotation of breech baby to cephalic by abdominal manipulation. Done at 36-37 weeks (earlier baby may turn back, later uterus too tight + fluid too low); 36w threshold for nulliparous, 37w for multiparous.

Success ~50% overall, ~70% with multiparity/posterior placenta/adequate liquor (DVP >3 cm)/non-engaged breech/operator experience.

After successful ECV, baby usually stays cephalic; failed ECV → planned CS at 39 weeks.
